channel.title: Justin Valentine
channel.description: Robots and the tools around them, by Justin Valentine.

item.title: A test suite for the haptic wrist
item.description: Bench results for the final haptic wrist on all three joints: friction, inertia, bandwidth, large-signal tracking, Z-width and virtual walls, with the WHAM prototype for comparison.

item.title: Sisyphus, a bike trainer app for the Mac
item.description: Runs a smart trainer in ERG mode from a small overlay that floats over full-screen video.

item.title: A haptic lightsaber game
item.description: Sword fighting on a WAM with the haptic wrist, where the arm pushes back when the blades meet, harder near the hilt than near the tip. How the force is computed, the opponents, the Meta Quest 3 viewer, and Barrett’s booth at IROS 2026.

item.title: The Alberta wrist
item.description: The last haptic wrist in the series, designed at Barrett Technology in 2026. From a cardboard model in May, through printed prototypes, to machined parts for two wrists and a set of spares, and Barrett’s booth at IROS in September, with the motor and ratio choices, the FEA and the measured results.

item.title: A Variable-Pitch Hopper
item.description: A screw cam whose groove sets the gear ratio, and the control board built around it.

item.title: Teaching the Hopper Where to Put Its Foot
item.description: A corner-balanced wheel triad, one-hop foot placement and softer landings, all in simulation.

item.title: Getting this site off the ground
item.description: Why this site is plain static pages.

item.title: Building the WHAM wrist
item.description: A two-joint, cable-driven haptic wrist for the WAM leader, with a thumb joystick for the follower’s last joint. My biggest machining project so far, from a printed version in January 2026 to the WAM in April.

item.title: A direct-drive end-effector wrist
item.description: A 3D-printed leader wrist for the WAM with three directly driven joints and a bike-grip handle. The operator holds it like an end effector, with nothing strapped to the arm. I demoed it at RISEx 2025.

item.title: The coaxial semi-differential wrist
item.description: A four-joint, cable-driven leader wrist for the WAM. Two of its drives are rings stacked around the forearm, and a fourth motor turns the whole wrist relative to the arm it’s mounted on.

item.title: Drawing sketches with guided flow matching
item.description: A course project that generates sketches point by point with flow matching and classifier-free guidance, then has a Barrett WAM draw them on a whiteboard that presses back with a constant force.

item.title: Writing DECtalk songs with an RNN
item.description: A character-level LSTM, trained on 1,085 DECtalk song files, that writes new songs for the old speech synthesizer to sing. A CMPUT 652 course project.

item.title: HAL, a quadruped with an actuated spine
item.description: A quadruped like Solo 8, with a motorized spine added so it might do a backflip, or a double. The figure-skater math behind the spine, a year of building, and HAL Gym for training it to flip.

item.title: A simple direct-drive gimbal wrist
item.description: A gimbal wrist for the WAM, driven directly so it was easy to prototype, that we used to test strapping the WAM to an operator’s forearm as an approximate exoskeleton.

item.title: A haptic mobile manipulator
item.description: A 7‑DOF WAM on a Clearpath Husky, driven from a second WAM so the operator feels what the robot touches. I designed the mobile base and set up the sensors and ROS. One of eight finalist teams in DND’s IDEaS challenge.

item.title: A spherical wrist after the Agile Eye
item.description: A three-motor spherical parallel mechanism I built as an idea for a haptic wrist, and why its Jacobian is the identity matrix at the home pose.

item.title: A 360° camera from six $20 action cameras
item.description: My CMPUT 428 final project with Justin Rozeboom. Six cheap action cameras in a laser-cut hexagonal housing on an iRobot Create 2, calibrated and stitched into cylindrical panoramas, plus a first try at structure from motion on the reprojected images.

item.title: A painting robot
item.description: My CMPUT 312 final project with Yash Bhandari. A six-servo arm from AliExpress on a wooden stand, painting SVG files onto a slanted canvas with a brush.

item.title: Go on a sphere
item.description: Go on a board with no edges or corners. I started it in 2022 while taking a differential geometry course, and finished it in 2026 as a playable game with a Monte Carlo tree search opponent.

item.title: A Rubik’s Cube solver
item.description: A Python program that simulates a cube of any size and solves the 3×3 with the beginner’s layer-by-layer method. I also started a webcam scanner for it in OpenCV.
